title: Fundamental Principles of State Policy (রাষ্ট্র পরিচালনার মূলনীতি)

articles.title: Fundamental principles
articles.content: The principles of nationalism, socialism, democracy and secularism shall constitute the fundamental principles of state policy.

articles.title: Nationalism
articles.content: The unity and solidarity of the Bangalee nation, which, deriving its identity from its language and culture, attained sovereign independence through a historic struggle, shall be the basis of Bangalee nationalism.

articles.title: Socialism and freedom from exploitation
articles.content: A socialist economic system shall be established with a view to ensuring the attainment of a just and egalitarian society.

articles.title: Democracy and human rights
articles.content: The Republic shall be a democracy in which fundamental human rights and freedoms and respect for the dignity and worth of the human person shall be guaranteed.

articles.title: Secularism and freedom of religion
articles.content: The principle of secularism shall be realised by the elimination of communalism, granting of political status in favour of any religion, and abuse of religion for political purposes.

articles.title: Provision of basic necessities
articles.content: It shall be a fundamental responsibility of the State to attain a steady improvement in the material and cultural standard of living of the people, by securing food, clothing, shelter, education and medical care.

articles.title: Free and compulsory education
articles.content: The State shall adopt effective measures for the purpose of establishing a uniform, mass-oriented and universal system of education and extending free and compulsory education to all children.
